verdict.summary: No provider review: register an OAuth app (or a GitHub App, which GitHub prefers) in Developer settings, paste Composio's callback URL, and real users can connect the same day.

addClaims.text: GitHub generally prefers GitHub Apps over OAuth apps; both use OAuth 2.0, but OAuth apps can only act on behalf of a user.
addClaims.quote: In general, GitHub Apps are preferred over OAuth apps. Both OAuth apps and GitHub Apps use OAuth 2.0.

addClaims.text: GitHub Apps use fine-grained permissions instead of the broad scopes OAuth apps use (e.g. reading code with an OAuth app needs the full repo scope).
addClaims.quote: GitHub Apps use fine-grained permissions. For example, if your app needs to read the contents of a repository, an OAuth app would require the repo scope

addClaims.text: Everything in the OAuth app registration is treated as public; GitHub warns against internal URLs or sensitive data.
addClaims.quote: Only use information in your OAuth app that you consider public. Avoid using sensitive data, such as internal URLs, when creating an OAuth app.

addClaims.text: Composio accepts your own GitHub App (client ID and secret in the GitHub auth config), not only an OAuth app.
addClaims.quote: You can bring your own GitHub App by configuring its client ID and client secret in the GitHub auth config.

addClaims.text: With a GitHub App, each user must still install the app and grant repository access; Composio does not yet send the installation link automatically.
addClaims.quote: Composio does not currently provide the GitHub App installation link automatically during this flow.

addBlockers.symptom: Connected via your GitHub App, but repository tools return 404 / 'Resource not accessible by integration'
addBlockers.cause: The user authorized the GitHub App but never installed it on the account or organization that owns the repositories (permissions come from the installation, not auth-config scopes).
addBlockers.fix: Send users your GitHub App's installation link (github.com/apps/<your-app>/installations/new) and have them select the repositories, then retry.
addBlockers.fallback: Use an OAuth app with the repo scope (broader access, no installation step), or Composio's managed GitHub app while prototyping.

addUncertainties: The 'Resource not accessible by integration' error text in the GitHub App blocker is GitHub's commonly reported message, not quoted from the cited pages.
